Steps in Character Creation

Choose an alignment, roll six ability scores in order, select a class that satisfies the prime requisite, then record hit points, armor class, saving throws, starting equipment and languages. Strength, Intelligence, Wisdom, Dexterity, Constitution and Charisma are scored from 3 to 18; the normal modifier is -3 at 3, -2 at 4-5, -1 at 6-8, none at 9-12, +1 at 13-15, +2 at 16-17 and +3 at 18. A prime requisite of 13 or better grants a 5% XP bonus; 9 or lower grants a 10% XP penalty.

Starting hit points are the maximum of the class hit die plus the Constitution adjustment; subsequent levels roll the hit die, with a minimum of 1 point. Starting gold is 3d6 x 10 gp. Characters begin with a languages score based on Intelligence and buy equipment from the Equipment chapter.

The Character Classes

Choose one class. A human may reach level 36 as a fighter, cleric, magic-user or thief; demihumans have lower maximum levels and class restrictions. A class supplies hit dice, attack progression, saving throws, experience requirements, spell access and special abilities.

ClassHit diePrime requisiteMax levelNotes
Clericd8Wisdom36Turn undead; cleric spells
Fighterd10Strength36Weapon mastery; no spells
Magic-Userd4Intelligence36Magic-user spells; read magic
Thiefd6Dexterity36Thief skills; backstab
Dwarfd8Constitution12Fighter abilities; detect tricks
Elfd6Intelligence10Magic-user spells plus fighter abilities
Halflingd6Dexterity8Fighter abilities; hiding and missile bonus

Multiclassing is not used. The optional Druid is an extension of the Cleric: it keeps cleric hit dice, saves and XP, but uses the druid spell list and druid restrictions. The Mystic is an optional variant handled by the DM.

Spells and Spellcasting

Spells are divided into nine levels and into the cleric, druid and magic-user lists. Clerics and druids receive spells through their deity; magic-users learn spells from spellbooks and need read magic to decipher them. A caster can only prepare the number of spells shown by the level table, and a spell is expended when cast.

A spell description gives range, duration, effect and often a saving throw. Reversible spells can be cast in an opposite form, usually with a saving throw allowed. Magical defenses modify saving throws, and anti-magic areas suppress spell effects.

Equipment

Coins weigh 10 per pound (100 cn), gems and jewels are carried separately, and each item has a cost in gold pieces and a weight in coin weight. Armor class is descending: unarmored AC 9, leather 7, scale 6, chain 5, banded 4, plate 3 and full plate 0. A shield subtracts 1 from AC.

Weapons list damage, range, cost and encumbrance; two-handed and missile weapons have the usual restrictions. Adventuring gear, transport and siege equipment are bought from the Equipment compendium.

Other Character Abilities

Weapon Mastery is optional. Humans receive weapon choices by level; demihumans begin with Basic skill in class-approved weapons. The five ranks are Basic, Skilled, Expert, Master and Grand Master. Each rank improves damage, range, attack bonus, defense or special effects as shown in the Weapon Mastery journal.

The optional General Skills system lets a character buy noncombat skills with weapon choices or skill points. The DM sets the characteristic and difficulty, then the player rolls d20 against the resulting target.

Movement

Exploration movement is measured in turns (10 minutes) and dungeon movement in rounds. Encumbered characters move more slowly; the movement rate is derived from total carried weight. Running increases speed but makes stealth impossible and can cause fatigue.

Water and air travel use their own tables for ships, rowing and flying speeds; weather and currents modify travel time.

Encounters and Evasion

When an encounter is possible, roll 2d6 for surprise (a result of 1-2 on a d6 can mean surprise for one side) and 2d6 on the monster reaction table. Hostile creatures may attack, parley or flee according to the result; the DM adjusts for obvious strength, alignment and previous conduct.

2d6Reaction
2-3Hostile, attacks immediately
4-5Hostile, may attack
6-7Neutral, uncertain
8-9No attack, may parley
10-12Friendly, helpful or enthusiastic

Wandering monsters are rolled by time and terrain. Evasion, pursuit and hiding use movement rates, surprise and the DM's judgment.

Combat

Each round: roll initiative (1d6 per side), resolve morale, movement, missile fire, spells and hand-to-hand attacks in order. To hit, roll d20 and compare the result to the attack matrix using THAC0 and the target's descending AC; a natural 1 always misses and a natural 20 always hits. Damage is rolled after a hit, modified by Strength for melee weapons.

CategoryCheckSuccess
Attackd20 + bonuses≥ THAC0 - AC
Saving throwd20≥ saving throw target
Ability checkd20≤ ability score + bonus
Morale2d6≤ morale score
Turn undead2d6≥ table cell

Morale is checked when foes die or when the situation turns against them. Unarmed combat deals 1d2 or 1d3 damage; grappling, disarming and called shots are optional. Spells cast in combat follow their listed casting time and range.

Mass Combat

For battles with many combatants, the War Machine converts each unit into a Combat Result using troop class, hit dice, morale and leaders. Opposing results are compared on the War Machine table to produce casualties, gains and losses. The Siege Machine resolves attacks on fortifications using class, armor and construction factors.

Leaders add their level and ability bonuses; terrain, surprise and morale can shift the result. The system resolves the battle as a whole rather than individual attacks.

Experience

XP is awarded for defeating monsters (the XP value in the monster entry), for treasure gained, for completing goals and for good role-playing. The DM divides awards among the characters who earned them. Partial levels are not used.

Constitution adjustmentHit points per level

Class maximum levels and demihuman level limits are enforced by the class tables in the Classes compendium.

Nonplayer Characters

Retainers and mercenaries are hired with pay, food and lodging. Their loyalty depends on the employer's Charisma, alignment, treatment and regular pay. Specialists such as sages, smiths and alchemists charge for services and may require contracts or advances.

Hirelings have morale scores and abandon or betray an employer when morale fails. The DM controls all NPC decisions, even when the players negotiate terms.

Strongholds and Dominions

A character can build a stronghold after reaching the appropriate level. Construction cost depends on size, materials and fortifications; monthly upkeep covers wages, supplies and repairs. Staff are hired from the NPC rules and have morale and loyalty.

A dominion generates income from taxes, trade and resources. The ruler must maintain order, collect taxes and defend the territory; population and attitude affect revenue.

Dungeon Master Procedures

When no specific rule applies, the DM sets a target number on d20 (easy 5, moderate 10, hard 15, very hard 20) and applies the relevant ability adjustment. Ability checks are optional; a natural 20 succeeds and a natural 1 fails when the DM uses that convention.

Aging modifies ability scores at thresholds determined by the DM. Alignment changes require a major shift in behavior and may cause the loss of class abilities. Anti-magic areas suppress spells and magical item powers. The DM's final ruling resolves ambiguous cases.

Monsters

Each monster entry lists armor class, hit dice, hit points, number appearing, movement, attacks, damage, special abilities, morale, treasure type and XP value. Hit dice are d8; a "+" adds hit points without changing the HD for attack or saving throw purposes.

Monsters use the same descending AC and saving throw categories as characters. Special attacks such as breath weapons, poison, paralysis and charm usually allow a saving throw with a stated modifier. Treasure type determines the rolled treasure.

Immortals

Immortal characters use spheres (matter, energy, time, space and thought) and ranks from novice to Hierophant. Each rank grants powers, higher ability scores and increased hit points, while requiring experience and a patron's approval.

Mortals may qualify through the paths of the Dynamism, the Hierarchy or the Void, each with different prerequisites. Immortal magic uses the same level structure but much larger energy costs.

Treasure

Treasure is generated by lettered types that specify coins, gems, jewelry and magical items. Gold, electrum, silver, copper and platinum have different values; gems and jewelry are valued individually and weigh less than coins.

Magical items include potions, scrolls, rings, wands, staves, swords, armor and miscellaneous items. Missile talents such as speaking, stunning, teleporting, transporting and wounding are separate from ordinary item powers. Creating an item costs gold and spell levels and requires a roll for success.

Campaigning

A campaign links adventures into a continuing world. The DM prepares key locations, factions, rumors and encounters, then adapts them to player choices. Consistent timekeeping, geography and NPC memory make the setting believable.

Use wandering monsters, random treasure and reaction checks sparingly so that the story remains coherent. Reward clever plans as well as combat, and let character actions change the world.

Combat Sequence

  1. Roll 1d6 for each side; the higher roll acts first.
  2. Check morale for NPCs and monsters.
  3. Move, then resolve missile fire, spells and hand-to-hand attacks.
  4. Apply damage and resolve special effects.

Attack: d20 + Strength/Dexterity + magic + mastery versus THAC0 - AC. Natural 1 misses; natural 20 hits automatically. Damage uses the weapon die plus Strength for melee attacks.

Attack Matrix

Read the row for the target's AC to find the needed modified d20 result. The dagger symbol marks an automatic hit on a natural 20; a natural 1 still misses.

Creating a magical item requires the caster to supply the spell levels, pay the gold cost and roll for success.

Weapon Mastery (Optional)

Weapon mastery lets a character study one weapon in depth, or several weapons less intensely. It is optional: the DM decides whether to use it. All characters, not only fighters, can learn it.

With these rules a human starts with no weapon skill and receives weapon choices. Demihumans start with Basic skill in all weapons allowed to their class, but do not gain weapon choices; they improve through training at levels 4, 8 and 12 (dwarves) and after maximum level.

A weapon choice buys one weapon used in one fashion. A bastard sword used one-handed and the same sword used two-handed are two separate choices. The net is a single exception.

Condensed reference from Rules Cyclopedia, Chapter 5.

Weapon mastery penalties with two weapons

CaseResult
Basic second weaponCannot be reduced below Basic

With the optional Two Weapons Combat rule, the second attack is at -4 to hit and is treated as one mastery level lower. A Basic second weapon stays Basic; an Unskilled weapon cannot be used as the second attack. Cestus, horned shield, knife shield and sword shield ignore the off-hand penalty; the tusked shield allows two attacks with no off-hand penalty. All optional sources together can add at most +1 attack per round.
